intent: Compare three card-back ideas through one Codex and one PixelLab interpretation of each idea.

concepts.label: The Arcane Relic
concepts.intent: An old, mysterious fantasy-game object with one iconic center: compelling to turn over, without borrowing recognizable trade dress.

concepts.label: The Fivefold Gambit
concepts.intent: Five occult powers surround a chessboard contest, making the arcane structure answer to the game’s actual play language.

concepts.label: The Closed Position
concepts.intent: Chess alone supplies the identity: mirrored armies, board geometry, and a sealed central square holding the hidden move.

candidates.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: universal game card back for a dark medieval chess tactics card game
Primary request: Concept 1, “The Arcane Relic” — an original card back based on what makes classic fantasy trading-card backs compelling: an ancient, handled game object with a mysterious central emblem and a sense of a vast hidden world. Do not reproduce any existing card back, logo, lettering, oval-and-five-dot layout, or recognizable trade dress.
Scene/backdrop: the artwork itself fills the entire straight-on vertical 5:7 card canvas edge to edge; no tabletop, no mockup, no surrounding environment.
Subject: a single ornate circular astrolabe-like reliquary at the exact center, nested rings of old brass and dark walnut, with five tiny mismatched mineral inlays integrated irregularly into the rings rather than evenly orbiting them; an abstract eclipsed star at the center.
Style/medium: richly painted dark-fantasy game art, tactile and aged, subtle hand-crafted asymmetry, premium physical-card finish.
Composition/framing: perfectly centered, vertically symmetrical overall, strong thumbnail silhouette, layered ornamental border, safe margin around all important detail, 5:7 portrait.
Lighting/mood: low amber glow from within the relic, mysterious, venerable, inviting.
Color palette: warm umber, blackened walnut, tarnished brass, muted mineral accents, restrained amber.
Materials/textures: worn leather, old wood grain, engraved brass, rubbed gilt, tiny scratches from play.
Constraints: original design; no text, letters, numbers, runes that resemble writing, logos, watermarks, chess pieces, hands, people, perspective tilt, cast shadow, exterior background, or card-face elements. The card back must be rotationally plausible and read cleanly at small size.

candidates.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: universal game card back for a dark medieval chess tactics card game
Primary request: Concept 3, “The Closed Position” — a pure chess-card-game identity with no fantasy trading-card vocabulary. Make the deck feel like a portable, secret chess position: formal, martial, and immediately legible as chess even at control-panel scale.
Scene/backdrop: the artwork itself fills the entire straight-on vertical 5:7 card canvas edge to edge; no tabletop, no mockup, no surrounding environment.
Subject: a perfectly mirrored heraldic composition built from an 8-by-8 board lattice, paired black and ivory knight profiles facing inward, compact rook crenellations anchoring all four corners, and one sealed empty central square as the hidden move. The chess forms should interlock into one ornamental back rather than look like loose pieces placed on a board.
Style/medium: richly painted medieval chess-set craftsmanship, restrained premium game-card ornament, graphic enough to read as a thumbnail.
Composition/framing: strict two-way symmetry, strong central axis, layered border based on board coordinates without letters or numbers, safe margin, 5:7 portrait.
Lighting/mood: sober torchlit tournament hall, controlled, intelligent, martial.
Color palette: ebony black, aged boxwood ivory, cold steel, a very restrained royal-purple thread, no rainbow gems.
Materials/textures: carved wood, hammered steel, worn wool baize, shallow engraved linework.
Constraints: original design; no arcane circles, colored power stones, celestial symbols, fantasy spell imagery, text, letters, numbers, notation, logos, watermarks, people, hands, perspective tilt, cast shadow, exterior background, or card-face elements. The card back must be rotationally plausible and read cleanly at small size.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: universal 5:7 game card back
Input images: Image 1 is the edit target and must remain recognizably the same “Closed Position” chess card-back candidate.
Primary request: Correct only the canvas geometry. Recompose Image 1 into an exact 5:7 portrait card back by expanding and rebuilding the artwork toward the left and right, so the entire existing top-to-bottom design remains visible. Do not crop away the top border, bottom border, corner rooks, any knight, or the central sealed square.
Composition/framing: exact 5:7 portrait rectangle, preferably 1060×1484; the complete outer card border must be visible on all four sides with a narrow, even safe margin; straight-on with no perspective. Preserve the same two-way mirrored heraldic arrangement, alternating ebony-and-ivory chess fields, paired knight profiles, four corner rooks, central sealed square, and ornamental steel/ivory border. Extend or proportionally reflow the side fields and ornament as needed to reach 5:7 without cutting anything off.
Style/medium: preserve Image 1’s richly painted medieval chess-set craftsmanship, materials, lighting, colors, texture, and level of detail.
Constraints: change only aspect ratio and the minimum geometry needed to fit it. Keep every major motif and the same visual identity. No new subjects, text, letters, numbers, notation, logos, watermarks, exterior background, tabletop, cast shadow, perspective tilt, or card-face content. The final image itself must be exactly 5:7, not a tall card floating inside a 5:7 background.

candidates.prompt: ONE SINGLE COMPLETE CHESS CARD BACK PANEL ONLY. The entire output is one vertical rounded 5:7 panel filling the canvas from edge to edge. Inside that one panel: strict two-way symmetry, paired black and ivory carved knight profiles facing inward, a small integrated checkerboard lattice, rook crenellations in the four corners, and one sealed empty square at the center. Formal medieval chess-set craftsmanship in polished pixel art. Ebony, aged ivory, cold steel, tiny restrained purple accents. No title, no words, no letters, no numbers, no logo, no game screen, no UI kit, no menus, no small cards, no characters, no castle scene, no dragon, no surrounding objects, no exterior background. Do not place the card inside another composition; the card back itself fills the whole panel.
